business_scope.primary_industry_name: Visual Web Template and Low-Code Web Application Builder

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: South Africa (national-level unitary corporate registry administered by the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC); no sub-state corporate registration distinctions)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Roman-Dutch common law foundation overlaid by English company-law doctrine, with the Constitution, 1996 supreme; company law governed by the Companies Act 71 of 2008)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: South Africa-United States Double Taxation Agreement (1997) covering income and enterprise profits; relevant to US-based SaaS payment rails (Stripe, Paddle)
South Africa-United Kingdom Double Taxation Agreement (2002, as amended by the 2014 protocol)
South Africa-People's Republic of China Double Taxation Agreement (2000)
SADC Protocol on Finance and Investment (2006) covering investment protection, capital transfer, and settlement of investment disputes among SADC member states
Southern African Customs Union (SACU) Agreement (2002) integrating customs and excise across South Africa, Botswana, Lesotho, Namibia, and Eswatini

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Companies Act 71 of 2008, sections 1 (definition of beneficial owner) and 56A; Companies Regulations 2011 (GN R351 of 26 April 2011), Regulations 33A-33C as inserted by the Companies Amendment Regulations 2023 (effective 1 October 2023); General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022; Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 (FICA), as amended by the Financial Intelligence Centre Amendment Act 1 of 2017, in particular sections 21A-21J, 28A, 29, and 42A; Protection of Constitutional Democracy Against Terrorist and Related Activities Act 33 of 2004 (POCDATARA).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (beneficial ownership information is filed with CIPC and is accessible by the Financial Intelligence Centre, South African Revenue Service, South African Reserve Bank, and other competent authorities; it is not a fully public register)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copies of the passport and proof of residential address of each proposed director, shareholder, and ultimate beneficial owner (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country passport/identity authority, certified by a notary public of the origin jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (South Africa acceded 30 April 1995; apostille issued by the origin country's competent authority per the Hague Convention of 5 October 1961) OR consular legalization by a South African embassy/consulate where the origin country is not a Convention member

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of legal existence / Certificate of Incumbency / company extract of any corporate shareholder holding 5% or more of the proposed shares
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or company secretary of the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, followed by a sworn English translation where the original is not in English

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (issued within 90 days) for each foreign corporate shareholder and foreign director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Equivalent corporate registry of the foreign jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille / consular legalization as above

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney authorizing the South African incorporation attorney to file the name reservation, incorporation application (CoR 14.1), and UBO declaration on behalf of non-resident subscribers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each non-resident shareholder/director executing before a notary public in their jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille / consular legalization; no further South African notarization is required where the original POA bears an apostille

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn English translation of all non-English passport, corporate, shareholding, and UBO documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Sworn translator accredited under the South African Magistrates' Courts Rules (High Court sworn translator)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Sworn affidavit plus notarial certification attached to the apostilled source document (the translation itself does not require a separate apostille)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference / source-of-funds letter covering the initial share capital contribution and operating funding of the Pty Ltd
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Account-holding bank of each UBO (to satisfy FICA due diligence for accountable institutions onboarding the company on Stripe/Paddle)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy plus apostille where the client bank or payment provider requires it

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, and authorized signatories against (i) the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, (ii) the South African targeted financial sanctions list administered by the South African Council for the Non-Proliferation of Weapons of Mass Destruction, (iii) the FIC published directives and domestic list of designated persons, and (iv) the US OFAC SDN list given the intended Stripe/Paddle payment rails. PEPs are defined in FICA s 1 as 'prominent public officials' (domestic and foreign, including family members and close associates) and require enhanced due diligence, senior management approval, and ongoing monitoring. Any match, attempted match, or suspicious transaction must be reported to the FIC within the prescribed forms and timeframes under FICA sections 28A and 29. The beneficial ownership calculus applies a 5% direct or indirect ownership/voting-rights threshold, plus control through other means, per FICA s 1 and Companies Act s 56A.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: CIPC online transactional platform (b2b.cipc.co.za) - e-Name Reservation under section 12 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008; direct filer and registered-agent channels are available through the CIPC electronic services portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names are accepted in English or any of the 11 official South African languages, but must be entered in Latin alphabet characters (A-Z) and Arabic numerals only, with restricted punctuation (e.g., ampersand, hyphen, apostrophe, comma, full stop); non-Latin script names must be transliterated into the Latin script. The CIPC name-search engine applies a token-based confusion screen and rejects names identical or confusingly similar to existing registered names, trademarks, or reserved names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: (1) On rejection, CIPC issues a name-rejection notice referencing the conflicting name or trademark; the applicant should request written reasons within 20 business days. (2) The applicant may re-file a new reservation with an amended distinctive element (e.g., a unique two-letter code or industry descriptor), or file a formal administrative appeal to the CIPC Name Evaluation and Appeals Unit within 30 days of rejection, attaching a trademark-search report, a consent letter from the conflicting name-holder, or evidence of acquired distinctiveness. (3) If the rejection is upheld, the applicant may apply to the Companies Tribunal under Companies Act section 160 (Form CTR 142) for a name determination. (4) Final recourse lies in an urgent High Court review under the Promotion of Administrative Justice Act 3 of 2000. Practically, the applicant may proceed with a revised name pending appeal if the appeal is not resolved within the 180-day reservation window; name reservations are not extendable as of right, so a fresh reservation filing is required upon expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted - a serviced or virtual office in a South African city (e.g., Johannesburg or Cape Town) satisfies the registered-office requirement under Companies Act section 23(3) provided it is a physical street address in South Africa where legal process and documents can be served and where relevant records remain accessible; a P.O. Box is not acceptable. For this low-risk no-code website builder industry, no additional operating licence requires a brick-and-mortar presence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low - estimated statutory or regulatory unannounced on-site inspection probability of less than 5% within the first 24 months given the ISIC 6201 low-risk profile, absent engagement in financial-services licensing or high-value cash flows; CIPC generally conducts documentary verification and postal compliance notices, while FIC/SARS inspections focus on high-risk accountable institutions and are triggered by reported anomalies.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: CIPC company name reservation fee (one name)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory CIPC tariff (ZAR 50; FX assumption 18.5 ZAR/USD)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, ss 13 (incorporation), 14 (registration), 15 (MOI), 19 (legal personality), 40 (share issuance); Companies Regulations, 2011, regs 7-14 and Forms CoR 9.1, CoR 14.1, CoR 14.2.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), established under s 185 of the Companies Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) accompanied by the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI) and registered via CIPC e-Services.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; s 19 abolishes par value and minimum capital. Shares may be issued for consideration permissible under s 40; no escrow account is mandated by law for ordinary private companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, by the incorporators, that the Memorandum of Incorporation filed with CIPC is adopted. RESOLVED FURTHER that, under section 40 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008, the subscriber shares be and are hereby allotted and issued. RESOLVED FURTHER that the registered office be fixed at the address recorded in the Notice of Incorporation. RESOLVED FURTHER that [Full Name] be and is appointed sole director, and [Full Name] company secretary, if statutorily required. RESOLVED FURTHER that the directors be authorized to open banking facilities and to file all CIPC, SARS, and municipal registrations. RESOLVED FURTHER that the first financial year-end be set; and that all ancillary acts before this resolution are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve Company Name and Verify Availability
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to CIPC e-Services, complete Form CoR 9.1 with two proposed names in priority order, pay the name reservation fee online, and submit. The applicant receives an automated reference number; name approval is granted electronically if no conflicting mark is found.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of incorporator's ID or passport
Signed power of attorney if submitted by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused, file a fresh CoR 9.1 with alternative names; CIPC retains no refund, so the applicant may refile immediately without prejudice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft Memorandum of Incorporation and Statutory Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator, company attorney, and notary public (notarization of MOI/power of attorney, if required)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the MOI in accordance with s 15 of the Companies Act, setting out share structure, director powers, and board quorum. Prepare consents to act as director and company secretary on Form CoR 14.2. Certified identity documents must be authenticated and, where foreign directors act, apostilled under the Hague Convention.
required_dossiers: Form CoR 14.2 (consent to act as director and company secretary)
Certified copies of directors' IDs or passports
Proof of registered office address (lease or title deed)
Apostilled documents for non-South African directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MOI is queried by CIPC, amend and resubmit with a covering note explaining the remedial clause; no fresh fee arises for a non-substantive correction within the same application reference.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Notice of Incorporation and Pay Registration Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services portal / CIPC Customer Contact Centre (accreditation counter)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Attach the approved name reservation, upload the MOI and Form CoR 14.1, and pay the CIPC registration fee. Confirm that the entity type is 'Private Company (Pty) Ltd'. On successful filing, CIPC issues a registration number with the suffix /07.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is rejected for verification failure, rectify the flagged discrepancy in the CIPC non-verification workflow and resubmit within the statutory correction period; escalate to the CIPC Verification Department if unresolved after two submissions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Incorporation Certificate and Open Statutory Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC (certificate issuance) and registered office custodian
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the electronic Certificate of Incorporation from e-Services. At the registered office, create the company seal (optional), minute book, share register, register of directors, register of beneficial owners, and a record of MOI amendments. These registers are mandatory under s 24 and the Companies Regulations.
required_dossiers: Register of directors and company secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains an error, lodge a request for rectification via e-Services with a supporting affidavit; CIPC will reissue the certificate without charge for registry-error corrections.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Convene First Board Meeting and Issue Share Certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors at registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold a statutory board meeting, adopt the pro-forma first board resolution, approve the issue of subscriber shares, and execute share certificates. Record the allotment in the share register and file any required share allotment return in CIPC, if applicable under the MOI.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the share issue is challenged for non-compliance with s 40, reconvene the board and pass a ratifying resolution documenting the consideration received; notify SARS and CIPC of the correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Beneficial Ownership Information and Complete Tax Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services and South African Revenue Service (SARS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within the statutory period after incorporation, submit the beneficial ownership declaration to CIPC under the Companies Amendment framework. Simultaneously register with SARS for Income Tax, VAT (if turnover threshold is met), and Pay-As-You-Earn (PAYE) as employer; obtain an Income Tax reference number.
required_dossiers: Directors' and beneficial owners' identity documents
Signed SARS registration forms (RA01 and VAT101 where applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC or SARS rejects the filing, correct the mismatched identifiers (e.g. ID numbers, addresses) and resubmit within the prescribed curing period; escalate to the CIPC Beneficial Ownership Unit or SARS branch manager if the query persists.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no industrial or manufacturing facility; the activity is a digital services business. Local municipal zoning approval suffices for office premises.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no national operating license is prescribed for no-code website building under ISIC 6201. A standard business license/trading certificate may be requested by the local metropolitan municipality.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — office-based software development does not appear on Listing Notices 1, 2 or 3 of the EIA Regulations, 2014; therefore no Environmental Authorisation or Basic Assessment is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial effluent discharge or VOC emissions. Company must comply with National Environmental Management: Waste Act 59 of 2008 for e-waste disposal; generators or cooling systems, if installed, must meet local air emission bylaws, otherwise below regulatory thresholds.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993: appoint a health and safety representative; obtain electrical Certificate of Compliance (COC) for leased premises; obtain fire extinguisher servicing certificate and emergency evacuation plan approval from the local Fire and Emergency Services department before staff occupancy.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) — official portal: SARS eFiling at https://www.sars.gov.za; physical registrations conducted at SARS branch offices nationwide.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A (Pty) Ltd incorporated under the South African Companies Act is automatically profiled by SARS for income tax upon receipt of CIPC incorporation data; the entity must activate the profile and obtain its Income Tax Reference Number via SARS eFiling within 21 business days of incorporation. Foreign-owned companies without local incorporation must appoint a representative taxpayer under s153 of the Tax Administration Act and obtain a non-resident income tax reference number. VAT registration: compulsory when taxable supplies exceed or are reasonably expected to exceed ZAR 1,000,000 in any 12-month period; voluntary registration available where taxable supplies exceeded ZAR 50,000 in the preceding 12 months. Registration is completed via SARS eFiling or a SARS branch using the CIPC registration number and supporting constitutional documents; a VAT vendor number is issued upon successful registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a South African-resident private company (Pty) Ltd is taxed at the corporate income tax rate of 27% (years of assessment ending on or after 1 April 2023) on worldwide income under the residence-based tax system; non-resident shareholders receive dividends subject to 20% dividends tax; no pass-through treatment is available; separate legal entity taxation applies with no group fiscal consolidation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists under South African law. Available statutory elections include: (1) Micro Business Turnover Tax election under the Sixth Schedule s4(2) for qualifying small businesses with annual turnover not exceeding ZAR 1,000,000 — irrevocable for two years and replacing normal income tax, VAT and dividends tax; (2) CFC high-tax election under s9D(9B) of the Income Tax Act to exclude a controlled foreign company's foreign income where effectively subject to tax in a foreign jurisdiction; (3) voluntary VAT registration election under s23(3) of the VAT Act; (4) hybrid mismatch arrangement adjustment elections under s8I–s8M with mandatory reporting; (5) s11(a) timing elections for certain deductible expenditure; (6) electronic services supplier VAT registration election. Entity classification itself is not elective and follows the statutory residence test under s1 of the Income Tax Act.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991, administered by SARS
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory registration: ZAR 1,000,000 taxable supplies in any consecutive 12-month period or reasonably expected to be exceeded in the following 12 months; Voluntary registration: ZAR 50,000 taxable supplies in the preceding 12-month period. Foreign suppliers of electronic services (including cloud-based no-code site builders) have no minimum turnover threshold and must register for VAT from the first supply of electronic services to South African residents under s54A of the VAT Act and the Electronic Services Regulations, unless wholly exempt.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: SARS imposes mandatory electronic filing through eFiling and SARS API channels for VAT returns, supporting documentation, and customs declarations. SARS is progressively implementing an e-invoicing framework aligned with OECD continuous transaction controls (CTC) and the SARS Modernisation Programme; a phased roll-out of real-time fiscal clearance with cryptographic integrity controls is underway, though universal mandatory real-time fiscal stamping is not yet fully operational. Vendors must issue full tax invoices within 21 days of supply under VAT Act s20, retain all electronic records for five years, and transmit invoice-level and transaction data to SARS upon its third-party data requests. The electronic services regime requires quarterly digital declaration of all supplies to South African recipients via the SARS eFiling/API channel with data-matching against payment rails (Stripe, Paddle), bank account details, IP addresses, and geolocation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods are zero-rated under s11(1)(a) of the VAT Act where goods are supplied to a non-resident and physically exported from South Africa within 90 days of the date of supply, supported by prescribed export documentation. Services, including software subscriptions, low-code platform access, and website builder services supplied to non-residents, qualify for zero-rating under s11(2)(l) if the recipient is outside South Africa and the services are not supplied for use or consumption in South Africa. Zero-rating does not apply to electronic services supplied to South African residents; those are subject to VAT at 15% under s54A with the place of supply determined by the recipient's usual residence, payment method, IP address, bank details, and SIM card country. The business must obtain documentary proof of the non-resident status of each customer and the foreign destination/use of the service.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD500) electronically lodged via SARS Customs EDI/ECS system
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill (original or electronic) evidencing physical export of goods
Commercial invoice and signed contract of sale indicating export terms and foreign buyer
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank foreign-exchange confirmation evidencing receipt of payment from abroad
Proof of foreign currency remittance showing repatriation of export proceeds
Delivery, packing, and shipment records confirming the goods left South Africa
Where applicable, proof of non-resident status of the service recipient (e.g., foreign registration details, passport, or payment rail confirmation)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS Customs conducts post-clearance verification and risk-profiling of zero-rated export declarations, cross-matching SAD500 data against VAT returns, bank FX records, and payment rail data. A claim of zero-rating that is unsupported by the prescribed documentation is rejected by SARS, triggering an additional VAT assessment at the standard rate of 15% on the full supply value under VAT Act s38, plus a 10% penalty and prescribed rate interest. Intentional or fraudulent zero-rating claims attract the understatement penalty regime under Tax Administration Act s223 (up to 200% of the shortfall), criminal prosecution with imprisonment of up to 60 months under VAT Act s59, deregistration from the VAT vendor roll, and retrospective clawback of refunds claimed together with compounded interest at the statutory prescribed rate. SARS routinely scrutinises export refunds before payment, and incomplete records result in refund suspension and audit.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) – Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), acting under the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933 (Act 9 of 1933) and the Exchange Control Regulations, 1961, as amended; prudential oversight of authorised dealers rests with the Prudential Authority (PA) of SARB established under the Financial Sector Regulation Act, 2017.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The ZAR is freely convertible for current-account transactions (software subscription fees, royalties, dividends, interest), with no SARB prior approval required for bona fide payments made via an Authorised Dealer. Capital-account inflows are liberally permitted: non-resident equity subscription into a South African (Pty) Ltd does not require prior FinSurv approval when the inward transfer is routed through an Authorised Dealer and reported in the eFinSurv system. Remittance hurdles for profits are modest: dividends must be declared out of realised profits, beneficial ownership must be evidenced, the 20% Dividend Withholding Tax (or treaty-reduced rate) must be settled, and the company must maintain a SARS tax compliance status for outward dividend processing; royalties and software licence fees to non-residents follow current-account rules with the applicable royalty withholding tax and supporting agreements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: All proceeds from exported services (SaaS licences and no-code subscriptions) must be repatriated to a South African account held with an Authorised Dealer within 180 days from the date of invoice or from the date of export performance. There is no mandatory conversion ratio: exporters may retain 100% of export earnings in a Foreign Currency Account (FCA) with no prescribed maximum retention period, and any conversion to ZAR occurs at the market rate through the Authorised Dealer. Each export receipt must be supported by commercial invoices and contracts and recorded in the bank's export-proceeds reporting return to FinSurv.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: The Standard Bank of South Africa Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational ZAR treasury account plus inward-investment holding/escrow account and Foreign Currency Account (USD/EUR/GBP) for export receipts
Operational ZAR business account plus FX managed account and Foreign Currency Account for cross-border receivable sweeps
Operational ZAR corporate account plus capital escrow sub-account for warehousing non-resident equity subscription funds
Operational ZAR account plus Foreign Currency Account and trade finance sweep products

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium as a supplementary collections and disbursement rail; Low as a primary banking substrate. Legal constraints: offshore digital EMIs (Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer, Mercury) are not licensed banks or Authorised Dealers under the Banks Act 94 of 1990, hold no direct domestic clearing access under the National Payment System Act 78 of 1998, and cannot provide a FICA-compliant ZAR local account for a South African entity. They may collect USD/EUR/GBP subscription revenue (including Stripe and Paddle payouts) and forward funds to the entity's Authorised Dealer account; any offshore account held by the SA company requires FinSurv approval through the dealer and full exchange-control reporting.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is legally possible for low-risk corporate clients under the FIC Act and its electronic verification amendments, but enhanced due diligence applies to foreign-resident directors and beneficial owners. In market practice, at least one director or a duly authorised attorney must attend a physical or hybrid customer interview at the selected Authorised Dealer's Johannesburg or Cape Town branch. Non-resident directors may alternatively complete verification through the bank's correspondent bank using notarised and apostilled or legalised identity documents, a certified copy of the CIPC beneficial-ownership filing, and a live video call; FNB and Nedbank selectively approve fully virtual onboarding for qualifying software exporters subject to a 6-month post-account transactional review.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity, including nominee holdings, discretionary trusts or an indirectly held foreign parent without a visible controller chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CIPC Beneficial Ownership Register extract (post-April 2023 filing), statutory share register, share subscription and shareholders' agreements, trust deed with trustee and beneficiary schedule, FICA declarations, and an ownership-chain diagram covering every shareholder above the 10% threshold.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient source-of-funds evidence for the inward capital injection, particularly where remittances originate from crypto-fiat exchanges or jurisdictions on the FATF grey list.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six months of remitter bank statements, contractual and valuation evidence supporting the subscription amount, SARS tax clearance and wealth-accumulation narrative, notarised source-of-wealth affidavit, and exchange withdrawal confirmations complemented by blockchain analytics where applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Substance mismatch: a no-code or SaaS exporter with few local employees, no board-activity record, and invoice flows that resemble a conduit or pass-through structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master subscription and distributor agreements, itemised invoices matched to the receivables ledger, hosting and domain registries in the company name, EMP201 and PAYE and UIF declarations for staff, VAT returns and ITR14 filings, board minutes, local lease or office evidence, and the recorded product URL with customer dashboard access.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or PEP hits on shareholders, counterparties or beneficiaries of outbound royalty and service payments, including unexplained name-alerts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: OFAC, UN, EU and UK consolidated screening results with date-stamped alert-resolution memos, PEP questionnaire and clearance letters, identity documents for all matching names, and legal-entity rationale plus confirming legal advice for any residual matches.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholders must wire funds by SWIFT MT103 to the company's account at a South African Authorised Dealer (AD), stating the ISO payment purpose and a clear remittance information block referencing 'Equity subscription – share capital' and the subscription agreement number. The AD verifies the remitter against the shareholder register, records the inflow in eFinSurv as inward foreign direct investment, and issues an inward transfer certificate that constitutes the exchange-control evidence for future dividend and capital repatriation flows. Funds may be held in the capital escrow sub-account until share subscription conditions are fulfilled; share certificates are issued only after cleared funds and the CIPC beneficial-ownership register is updated.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: SaaS disbursements use: (i) domestic ZAR EFT and ACH rails (MIP under the National Payment System Act 78 of 1998) for local vendors, payroll and SARS; (ii) regional SACU and Common Monetary Area settlements via SWIFT MT103 in ZAR for Namibia, Lesotho and Eswatini counterparties; (iii) international vendor and contractor payments (hosting, cloud, legal, licensing) via SWIFT MT103 with underlying invoices and the current-account declaration submitted to the AD, plus SARS tax-clearance confirmation where required for the payment class; (iv) commercial letters of credit, documentary collections and bank guarantees for any physical procurement or reseller-finance arrangements; and (v) card and scheme rails (Stripe Billing, Paddle) for global customer collections, with periodic conversion and repatriation sweeps closed out through the AD account.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward exchange contracts (FECs) on USD/ZAR, GBP/ZAR and EUR/ZAR to hedge confirmed subscription revenue and vendor cost exposures
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on ZAR where the underlying exposure exceeds deliverable limits or ZAR settlement is constrained
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for long-dated balance-sheet hedging of USD future obligations against ZAR revenue streams
Vanilla currency options, collars and zero-cost structures on USD/ZAR treasury exposures
FX spot and swap conversions executed within the Authorised Dealer facility for treasury cash-flow management

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Annual Return (Companies Act 2008, s 33; Companies Regulations 2009, reg 33)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), South Africa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary date of incorporation; the annual return period follows the company's registration anniversary.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late annual return penalties accrue per the prescribed CIPC fee schedule; persistent failure to file for two consecutive annual return cycles allows CIPC to issue a compliance notice and commence administrative deregistration after 30 business days' notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (AFS) and, if triggered, audited or independently reviewed statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: CIPC for companies with a mandatory audit or independent review; otherwise AFS retained at the registered office for CIPC inspection on demand.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the financial year-end; where audit or review applies, the signed AFS are filed with CIPC together with or before the annual return.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to prepare and deliver AFS within the prescribed period is a compliance contravention under Companies Act ss 30 and 33; CIPC may issue a compliance notice, impose administrative fines, and use continued non-compliance to support deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Declaration (UBO annual confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually with the CIPC annual return, within 30 business days after the incorporation anniversary; updates required within 30 days after any shareholding or beneficial ownership change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or maintaining a false beneficial ownership declaration is an offence under the Companies Act; CIPC may reject the annual return, issue a compliance notice, and hold directors personally liable for administrative penalties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent annual audit applies when the Public Interest Score (PIS) is at least 500. Independent review applies when PIS is at least 100 and below 500, unless the AFS are prepared by an independent accounting professional in accordance with regulation 28. A company with PIS below 100 may prepare and retain internally compiled AFS without audit or review. PIS is calculated under the Companies Regulations: 1 point per employee, 1 point per ZAR 1 million of turnover, 1 point per ZAR 1 million of third-party liabilities, and 1 point per shareholder or known beneficial owner.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as issued by the IASB, or IFRS for SMEs, as adopted in South Africa; the applicable framework must produce a true and fair view of the company's affairs.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain a Register of Beneficial Ownership accessible to CIPC. On each annual filing cycle, the board must confirm all persons holding beneficial interests in the company's issued securities. Any shareholding transfer during the year must be recorded in the register and reported to CIPC within 30 days of the transaction; without this confirmation, the annual return is treated as incomplete and CIPC may reject the filing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Shareholder and Director Resolutions
Register of Prescribed Officers and Company Secretary (if appointed)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 120 - USD 350 typical annual range for registered office, company secretarial, and CIPC filing agent services for a low-risk proprietary limited company
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 - USD 12,000 typical certified audit fee range for a small-scale technology company if an audit becomes mandatory; not applicable where the Public Interest Score remains below the audit threshold

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (applicable rate for years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023; standard rate reduced from 28%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday regime exists for (Pty) Ltd companies. Available preferences under the Income Tax Act 58 of 1962: s 11D R&D enhanced deduction (150%); s 12B accelerated renewable-energy wear-and-tear (solar PV, wind, biomass); s 12C accelerated manufacturing asset allowance; s 12L energy-efficiency allowance (45% of qualifying savings); small-business corporation (SBC) progressive rates only for qualifying entities with annual turnover below the prescribed threshold (not applicable to a standard Pty Ltd acting as a no-code site builder unless it qualifies).
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (no statutory time limit under s 20(1)(a)). For years of assessment commencing on or after 1 January 2022, the deduction of an assessed loss is capped at 80% of taxable income per annum.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IRP6 (Provisional Tax Return) — filed exclusively via SARS eFiling; mandatory for all resident companies including (Pty) Ltd.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Semi-annual: first provisional return at the 6-month mark of the year of assessment; second provisional return at year-end; optional third 'top-up' return within 6 months after year-end.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Year of assessment runs 1 March to 28/29 February. First provisional payment and return: on or before the last business day of the 6th month of the assessment year (31 August for a February year-end). Second: on or before the last business day of the year of assessment (28/29 February). Third top-up: within 6 months after year-end (voluntary, recommended to limit interest exposure).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reasonable estimate of the current year's taxable income; must be benchmarked against the 'basic amount' (prior year taxable income) adjusted for non-recurring items and known changes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not applicable to non-resident shareholders; the resident company makes the estimate on its own worldwide income. A non-resident director's remuneration is excluded unless South African services are rendered.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the 27% statutory rate to estimated taxable income in respect of the full year of assessment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No individual rebates or PAYE credits apply at this line; amounts withheld on behalf of the company are credited separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduct employees' tax (PAYE) paid to SARS on the company's behalf, foreign tax credits (s 6quat), and any assessed carry-forward credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign withholding taxes borne by the company on cross-border interest or royalty income may be claimed here, subject to the s 6quat cap.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Difference between estimated annual tax and prepaid credits; remit to SARS with the IRP6. Under-estimation triggers a 20% shortfall levy unless the estimate is at least 80% of actual taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No non-resident shareholder filing obligation arises at this stage.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Under-estimation of provisional tax: additional 20% levy on the shortfall (increased to 25% where the estimate is less than the basic amount) plus prescribed interest. Late or non-filing: monthly administrative penalty under s 210 TAA (10% of assessed tax for the first month and 5% per subsequent month, capped at 35 months, with a minimum monthly amount of ZAR 250–2,000 depending on turnover). Criminal default: fine and/or imprisonment up to 12 months under s 234 TAA.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 (Company Income Tax Return) — filed via SARS eFiling; mandatory for all resident companies regardless of turnover.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, aligned to the company's financial year-end (typically 28/29 February for South African (Pty) Ltd companies).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The ITR14 must be submitted within 12 months of the end of the year of assessment. SARS eFiling pre-populates and may issue an auto-assessment for certain companies; the taxpayer must verify and finalise within the prescribed window.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section A – Company particulars and Public Officer
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company registration number, date of incorporation, trade and registered address, tax reference number, and the appointed Public Officer's identity and contact details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A resident Public Officer must be appointed within one month of incorporation under s 246 TAA, even where all directors are non-resident; a non-resident may not serve as Public Officer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section B – Gross income and recoupments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare all amounts received or accrued, including South African and foreign-source income; residents are taxed on worldwide income. Include recoupments of previously claimed deductions (e.g., sale of fixed assets).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A resident (Pty) Ltd must declare global revenue; non-resident shareholders do not report their share of retained earnings.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim only expenses incurred in the production of income under s 11(a) and specific allowances (s 11D, s 12B, s 12C, s 12L). Disallow non-deductible items: capital expenditure, fines, dividends, and expenses not supported by records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to non-resident related parties (royalties, interest, service fees) must be arm's-length and may be subject to withholding taxes; non-deductible if the s 31 transfer-pricing requirements are not satisfied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section D – Assessed loss brought forward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Carry forward the assessed loss from the prior tax period; apply the 80% utilisation cap for years of assessment commencing on or after 1 January 2022.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No special non-resident treatment; the loss belongs exclusively to the resident taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section E – Taxable income and normal tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute taxable income after deductions and loss set-off; apply the 27% corporate rate to arrive at normal tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The resulting tax is an entity-level liability; it is not imputed to shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section F – Credits, prepayments and balance
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduct PAYE credits, provisional tax payments, and foreign tax credits (s 6quat). The net balance is payable to SARS or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No foreign tax credit is available to a non-resident shareholder on the company's income; such credits only attach to the shareholder's domestic return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose dividends declared during the year; reconcile the 20% Dividends Withholding Tax (DWT) paid via the separate dividend return and payment schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividends paid to non-resident shareholders trigger DWT at 20% unless treaty relief is supported by a valid Declaration and Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) retained by the company.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: monthly s 210 TAA penalty (10% of tax for the first month plus 5% per month thereafter, capped at 35 months; minimum monthly amounts of ZAR 250–2,000 apply where no tax is payable). Understatement penalty (s 222–223 TAA): 10%–150% of the shortfall depending on the conduct category. Interest: compounded daily at the prescribed SARS rate. Criminal default: s 234 TAA fine and/or imprisonment up to 12 months; deliberate false return under s 235 TAA: fine and/or imprisonment up to 5 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% under s 64E of the Income Tax Act, levied on dividends paid by the (Pty) Ltd to non-resident beneficial owners. The company acts as statutory withholding agent, must withhold before payment, and must remit DWT to SARS within 30 days of the dividend payment. Failure to withhold renders the company personally liable for the tax, interest and penalties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before declaring or paying a dividend to a non-resident shareholder, the company must obtain and retain: (1) a signed SARS-prescribed Declaration by the Beneficial Owner; (2) an original or certified copy of the Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the shareholder's tax authority for the relevant year; and (3) documentary evidence of the shareholding percentage supporting the reduced treaty rate. The documentation must be retained for five years and produced to SARS on demand. If documentation is incomplete, the full 20% statutory rate must be withheld. Treaty rates for dividends under South African DTAs commonly range from 0% to 15% (e.g., 5% for shareholdings of 10% or more; 7.5%–10% for portfolio holdings).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory rate 15% (s 49A–49G ITA); treaty rates commonly 5%–12% (some DTAs provide 0% for pure copyright royalties). Interest: statutory rate 15% (s 50A–50H ITA) with exemptions for listed debt instruments and certain government bonds; treaty rates commonly 0%–10%. Relief requires the same TRC-backed beneficial-owner declaration; the payer must withhold at the statutory rate unless valid treaty documentation is held before payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: mandatory when aggregate 'international related party transactions' (IRP transactions) entered into by the South African company in a year of assessment exceed ZAR 100 million. Master File and Country-by-Country Report: required where the multinational group's consolidated annual revenue exceeds ZAR 10 billion. The IRP6 provisional return requires a transfer-pricing declaration indicating whether TP documentation applies.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Africa does not operate a separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) statute comparable to offshore hubs; however, economic substance is legally embedded in: (1) tax residence (incorporation plus 'place of effective management' under the definition of 'resident' in s 1 ITA); (2) the s 31 transfer-pricing rules requiring a functional analysis of assets, risks and people functions; (3) the CFC regime (s 9D), which attributes passive income to South Africa unless the foreign subsidiary demonstrates adequate local substance; and (4) the General Anti-Avoidance Rules (s 80A–80L), which void 'impermissible avoidance arrangements' lacking commercial substance. Treaty benefits may similarly be denied where a company or intermediary is a mere conduit without substance or qualifies as a non-beneficial owner. A no-code website builder (Pty) Ltd acting as a UAE-route IP holder or payment intermediary without local staff, premises or risk capacity will fail substance scrutiny.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly submitting an ITR14 that understates gross income or inflates deductions; issuing or using false invoices; destroying or concealing accounting records; failing to register as a taxpayer; misrepresenting the company's revenue or the source of income to SARS.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal offence under s 235 TAA: fine and/or imprisonment up to 5 years per count. Civil understatement penalty under s 222–223 TAA: 150% of the shortfall for intentional tax evasion (10%–25% for lesser conduct categories). Compounded daily interest at the prescribed rate attaches to the full assessed shortfall. The company may also be deregistered and its tax clearance certificate withdrawn.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the Public Officer who knowingly participated face joint criminal prosecution; SARS may recover unremitted PAYE, DWT, or VAT from directors personally under s 179 TAA; director disqualification under the Companies Act; personal estate sequestration; court-ordered travel bans may be obtained under s 194 TAA for outstanding tax debt.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Continuing to trade while insolvent; using the (Pty) Ltd as a sham or façade to divert personal income or strip assets; backdating agreements; paying dividends while outstanding tax liabilities remain; using company funds as a personal bank account while leaving SARS unpaid.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Companies Act 71 of 2008 s 77(3) read with s 22: court may declare the director personally liable for the company's debts, including SARS claims, without a limitation cap; the corporate veil is piercable under s 20(9) where the company's juristic personality is abused; the transaction may be set aside as a voidable preference under insolvency rules if within 6 months of liquidation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for company tax debts; disqualification from serving as a director for up to 10 years; sequestration of personal assets; SARS may attach and sell assets personally; a director who deliberately obstructs the collection process may be imprisoned.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing the (Pty) Ltd or an offshore sister entity with no employees, no premises, no decision-making capacity, and no risk-bearing function, purely to channel royalty, interest, or service income into a favourable DTA jurisdiction, to access a reduced dividend withholding rate, or to defer South African taxation; circular loans; artificially inflated management fees; parking of IP income in a zero/low-tax affiliate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disregard of the transaction under s 31 TP rules and s 80A–80L GAAR; recomputation at the arm's-length price; denial of interest deductions on interest-free or below-market 'financial assistance' under s 31(3); assessment of 27% corporate income tax on imputed income; 20% DWT on deemed dividends; 15% WHT on deemed royalties/interest; understatement penalties up to 150%; compound interest. The arrangement may also be cleared under the principal purpose test in the applicable treaty, eliminating the reduced withholding rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who designed or executed the sham arrangement are personally liable for the assessed shortfall where the veil is pierced; criminal exposure if false statements or artificial documents were submitted; SARS may issue a notice of civil recovery against directors and connected persons; travel bans and asset freezes are available during investigation, and cross-border mutual assistance procedures may expose assets held abroad.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / FICA Non-Compliance and Money Laundering
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing payments or subscription revenues for known sanctioned persons or criminal enterprises through the no-code platform or via Stripe/Paddle rails; deliberately ignoring red flags in merchant records; structuring transactions to avoid FIC reporting thresholds; failing to file Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) where an employee or director knows or suspects that funds in the corporate bank account are proceeds of crime; operating as an unregistered accountable institution if the corporate scope expands into payment facilitation, money transfer, or financial services without FIC registration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Prevention of Organised Crime Act 121 of 1998 ss 4–6: fine up to ZAR 100 million and/or imprisonment up to 30 years. Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001: administrative sanction up to ZAR 10 million per contravention; criminal penalty for failure to report a suspicious transaction: fine and/or imprisonment up to 15 years. SARS penalty loading of 150% applies where evasion is connected to illicit flows.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and senior managers are personally liable if they knowingly failed to implement AML controls or permitted the business to be used for laundering; FIC administrative fines and criminal sanctions attach personally; bank accounts may be frozen; personal travel bans and extradition are possible under international mutual legal assistance; personal sequestration follows.
